articles.title: Composite graft survival in allen zone II fingertip amputations: Independent predictors of graft failure.
articles.authors: Gurhan U, Kahve Y, Sari E, Umur FL
articles.population: Patients with Allen Zone II fingertip amputations treated with composite grafting
articles.outcomes: Graft survival at 6 weeks postoperatively; graft failure defined as necrosis affecting more than 25% of graft surface area
articles.take_home: Diabetes and crush or avulsion type injuries are the strongest predictors of composite graft failure in fingertip amputations. Time from injury to surgery over 4.3 hours was associated with failure, though other factors were more important when considered together.

articles.title: Collagen nanofibers enhanced by plasma rich growth factors (PRGF) for the burn wound healing.
articles.authors: Abedini-Esfahlani M, Khodabakhshi MR, Eslami-Mahmoudabadi M, Nourani MR
articles.population: Male Wistar rats with full-thickness burn wounds
articles.outcomes: Wound closure rate, re-epithelialization, inflammation levels, fibroblast infiltration, collagen deposition, and VEGF expression over 21 days
articles.take_home: Collagen nanofibers containing plasma rich growth factors (PRGF) significantly accelerated burn wound healing in rats compared to standard treatment, with better skin regrowth and tissue repair. This laboratory finding suggests PRGF-enhanced nanofibers could be a promising wound dressing for severe burns, though human studies would be needed to confirm this.

articles.title: Application of a dynamic wound closure device in orthopaedic trauma patients following fasciotomy: A level-1 trauma center perspective and preliminary case series.
articles.authors: Pearce O, Lefaivre KA, Broekhuyse HM, Sepehri A, Stockton DJ, Guy P, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients who had undergone fasciotomy
articles.outcomes: Achievement of delayed primary closure of fasciotomy wounds using a dynamic wound closure device
articles.take_home: A dynamic wound closure device that uses the skin's natural elasticity may help close difficult fasciotomy wounds without needing more complex soft-tissue reconstruction surgery. The device gradually brings wound edges together on the ward, potentially improving both healing and appearance.

articles.title: Use of the National Trauma Data Bank in orthopaedic trauma research: a bibliometric analysis.
articles.authors: Beiene ZA, Conley RTA, Marmor MT
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma research studies using the National Trauma Data Bank
articles.outcomes: Trends in research publication, institutional participation, journal representation, injury types studied, and research themes in orthopaedic trauma
articles.take_home: The National Trauma Data Bank is being increasingly used for orthopaedic trauma research, with most studies focusing on pelvis, spine and lower limb fractures whilst shoulder injuries and soft tissue injuries remain understudied areas.

articles.title: Risk factors for scaphoid nonunion in acute fractures treated with cast immobilization.
articles.authors: Dean BJF, Saedi F, Riley ND, Ather S, Tsegaye B, Dhiman P, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients aged 16 years and over with acute scaphoid fractures treated with cast immobilisation
articles.outcomes: Union or nonunion of scaphoid fracture assessed by CT scan
articles.take_home: Scaphoid fractures were less likely to heal if the bone pieces were shifted apart by 1 mm or more, with risk roughly tripling. Interestingly, younger adults aged 26 to 36 years had the highest risk of nonunion, whilst older patients had much lower risk.

articles.title: Impact of the hybrid emergency room system on long-term functional outcomes in severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.authors: Mitsuyama Y, Umemura Y, Nishida T, Watanabe A, Nakamoto N, Kiguchi T, et al.
articles.population: Patients with severe traumatic brain injury (Head Abbreviated Injury Scale ≥3, Glasgow Coma Scale ≤8)
articles.outcomes: Long-term functional status measured by Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOS-E) at follow-up and discharge; secondary outcomes included psychological and quality-of-life measures
articles.take_home: Patients treated in a hybrid emergency room where imaging, interventional radiology and surgery were in one suite had better long-term functional outcomes than those treated in a conventional emergency room. The hybrid system reduced time to imaging and surgery, and patients were more likely to achieve favourable functional recovery.

articles.title: Histologic and physiologic effects of PRP and HBO on muscle healing after contusion injury in an animal model.
articles.authors: Chen P, Chiu JC, Lei KF, Chen SC, Chan YS
articles.population: C57BL6J mice with induced muscle contusion injury
articles.outcomes: Number of regenerating muscle fibres, muscle weight, fast-twitch strength and tetanic strength
articles.take_home: In mice, platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection and hyperbaric oxygen therapy both improved muscle healing after contusion, with the combination of both treatments potentially working together to restore muscle strength to near-normal levels. Hyperbaric oxygen alone also showed benefits but these were smaller than with PRP treatment.

articles.title: Reliability of patient and proxy reported pre-injury functional status in orthopaedic trauma: A prospective observational study.
articles.authors: Kelly R, Hong I, Mucharraz C, Taylor L, Bajwa S, Joyce C, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with acute upper or lower extremity fractures attending a level I trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Reliability of retrospective patient and proxy-reported pre-injury functional status using PROMIS CAT surveys at weeks 0, 2 and 6 post-injury
articles.take_home: Patients can accurately remember how well they were functioning before their injury, even up to 6 weeks after the fracture. When patients cannot report themselves, a family member or carer can provide similarly reliable information about their pre-injury function.

articles.title: "Feeling seen, not judged": Stakeholder experiences during early implementation of a trauma collaborative care model for socially vulnerable survivors.
articles.authors: Montoya-Rubiano MA, Stoeger E, Herrera-Escobar JP, Zier C, Foley K, Hoffman A, et al.
articles.study_type: Qualitative study of early implementation experiences
articles.population: Trauma survivors (socially vulnerable), trauma centre staff, and community partners
articles.outcomes: Patient experiences of feeling heard, engagement through provider adaptation, need for sustained mental health support, implementation challenges
articles.take_home: A new collaborative care model for vulnerable trauma survivors helped patients feel listened to and supported beyond their initial surgery. The model worked best when staff adapted their approach to individual patient needs and provided long-term mental health support.

articles.title: The evolution of a novel technique for treatment of intercostal hernias and restoration of costal margin rupture.
articles.authors: Sharma R, Rafael A, Pailthorpe C, Bhattarai K, Leong JY, Sayed S
articles.population: Patients with intercostal hernias and costal margin rupture
articles.outcomes: Successful repair of costal margin rupture using titanium bar with rotatable connectors mounted on titanium rib clips
articles.take_home: A new surgical technique using titanium components successfully repaired chest wall hernias in these three patients, with earlier diagnosis through better imaging leading to better outcomes than delayed diagnosis.

articles.title: Navigated percutaneous column screw fixation combined with total hip arthroplasty for non-reconstructable acetabular fractures in geriatric patients.
articles.authors: Pozzi L, Wahl P, Kuttner H, Nehls F, Schlappi M, Meier C
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over with non-reconstructable acetabular fractures treated with navigated percutaneous screw fixation and total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality 10%, revision rate 12%, 69% returned to previous living environment, 65% regained pre-traumatic walking abilities, cup loosening in 5% at median 7.3 months follow-up
articles.take_home: This surgical technique combining screw fixation with hip replacement allowed most elderly patients with complex hip fractures to return home and walk as before their injury. The approach minimises surgical burden while providing a stable hip that allows immediate weight bearing.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in the evaluation and treatment of osteoporotic and fragility fractures: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Liu X, Chui ECS, Wu X, Wang Y, Li T, Xie T, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of artificial intelligence applications
articles.population: Adults with osteoporotic and fragility fractures
articles.sample_size: 21 studies included in the systematic review
articles.outcomes: Fracture risk prediction, bone mineral density estimation, osteoporosis screening, fracture detection, and postoperative outcome prognosis
articles.take_home: Artificial intelligence tools show promise in predicting fracture risk and diagnosing osteoporosis, often performing better than traditional methods like FRAX. However, most studies need better validation with more patients and centres before these tools can be reliably used in daily clinical practice.

articles.title: Reliability and reproducibility of classification of distal ulnar fractures using cone beam computed tomography (CBCT).
articles.authors: Wreto L, Fornander L, Kammerling N, Nyman E, Moloney M
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study of classification system reliability
articles.population: Patients with distal ulnar fractures who underwent cone beam computed tomography scanning
articles.outcomes: Reliability and reproducibility of AO/OTA and Biyani classification systems using kappa value analysis
articles.take_home: Both classification systems for distal ulnar fractures showed reasonable consistency when used repeatedly by the same observer but were not reliable enough for dependable clinical use, suggesting that new classification approaches may be needed for these fractures.
